title: USWNT stars Megan Rapinoe, Julie Ertz voted into National Soccer Hall of Fame
content:
Former U.S. women’s national team stars Megan Rapinoe and Julie Johnston Ertz have been elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility, the organization announced on Thursday,

The two-time World Cup winners headline the 2027 class, alongside England and Manchester United great David Beckham, former U.S. men’s national team striker Jozy Altidore, indoor soccer legend Tatu from Brazil and former USMNT and LA Galaxy coach Lothar Osiander. The group will be honored at a ceremony at Toyota Stadium in Frisco, Texas, in April 2027.

Rapinoe, Ertz and Altidore were elected from the player ballot, each receiving 46 of 48 possible votes, or 95.8 percent, in their first year of eligibility. Beckham and Tatu were chosen via the veteran ballot, and Osiander through the builders ballot.

For Rapinoe and Ertz, the recognition comes three years after they ended their international careers, closing a chapter in which the USWNT won back-to-back World Cups in 2015 and 2019. They were central to one of the most successful periods in USWNT history.

Ertz, who played as both a defender and defensive midfielder, was a backbone of the team. She made 123 appearances between 2013 and 2023, scoring 20 goals, and appeared in three World Cups and two Olympic Games.

Her versatility became one of her defining qualities. After helping the U.S. win the 2015 World Cup as a center back, she moved into midfield and became a key part of the team’s successful title defense four years later. She was named U.S. Soccer’s Female Player of the Year in 2017 and 2019.

At the club level, the now 34-year-old spent much of her professional career with the then Chicago Red Stars before joining Angel City in 2023. She earned NWSL Best XI honors in 2019.

Rapinoe’s legacy goes beyond her contributions on the field. One of the most recognizable figures in women’s soccer, she became a leading voice for equal pay, LGBTQ+ rights and social justice while helping elevate the profile of the women’s game in the United States.

On the field, she made 203 appearances for the USWNT between 2006 and 2023, scoring 63 goals and competing in four World Cups.

Rapinoe’s defining tournament came at the 2019 edition in France, where she won both the Golden Boot as the competition’s leading scorer and the Golden Ball trophy as its best player. Over the following months, global soccer governing body FIFA named her Women’s Player of the Year and the now 41-year-old became the only American (male or female) to win the Ballon d’Or, the prestigious award given to the best player of the previous year by the French sports publication L’Equipe.

Rapinoe started playing professionally for Chicago Red Stars in now-defunct Women’s Professional Soccer (WPS) in 2009. After playing for a handful of teams in that competition, she became a central figure for Seattle Reign in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) from 2013 until her retirement in 2023. She played on loan for half of the 2012-13 season with Lyon in France.

While Ertz and Rapinoe were selected in their first year of eligibility, the hall’s 2027 election left several prominent names out, including two other members of the USWNT’s World Cup-winning generation.

Every year, 20 player finalists are selected to receive votes from the 48-member player voting committee.

Ali Krieger, another two-time World Cup champion who retired in 2023 after winning the NWSL championship with Gotham FC, received 43 votes, or 89.6 percent, in her first year of eligibility. She finished level with former USMNT captain Michael Bradley, but behind Rapinoe, Ertz and Altidore, who occupied the three available player ballot spots.

Sam Mewis, another member of the 2019 World Cup-winning squad, got 35 votes, or 72.9 percent, falling short for a second consecutive year. Mewis had 32 votes, 66.7 percent, in the 2026 election.
